message.subject: Receipt for my September payment
message.body:
Good morning,

I would be grateful if you could send me a receipt for my September payment of $118.00, which was taken on the 5th of September. The receipt number on your email is CHG-30028.

I like to keep a paper copy of all my medical expenses in a folder for my records, and I would prefer the receipt to show my name and home address. The ones I have received so far only show my email address.

My address is 2 Waratah Close, Chatswood NSW 2067. My Medicare number is 6492 30720 1, in case you need it to find my details.

Thank you for your help.

Kind regards,
Grace Papadopoulos

policy.label: Policy P5.1: Plan charges, billing dates and receipts
policy.text:
A monthly plan is charged on its billing date, which is the same day each month as the day the plan started, in the patient's local currency. The charge covers the prescribed products for that month, standard delivery and follow-up consults.

A receipt is emailed after every charge. Patients can download copies from Billing in their account, and support can resend any receipt or add the patient's address to it.

A card check (pre-authorisation) can appear as a pending amount for up to 5 business days before it drops off. It is not a second charge.

Patients can move their billing date once every 3 months. The first charge on the new date covers the days in between, pro rata. Patients update their card in their account under Billing; support never takes card numbers by chat or email.

policy.label: Policy P11.1: Product questions
policy.text:
Storage. Keep products below 25°C, out of direct sunlight, in their original packaging with the lid closed tightly, and out of reach of children and pets. They do not need to go in the fridge unless the label says so. Do not leave them in a car. Some oils can thicken or look cloudy when cold.

If a product looks, smells or tastes different, has been left somewhere hot, or a spray or dropper is not working, ask the patient not to use it until a pharmacist has checked. A pharmacist contacts them within 1 business day and arranges a replacement if needed. Agents never say a product is safe, fine or OK to use. If the patient asks whether it is still safe or OK to use, that is a clinical question: it goes to the clinician queue with no drafted reply (see clinical questions).

Packaging. Orders arrive in plain outer packaging. The label shows the patient's name and address only; it does not name the product or say it is medicine.

Availability and substitutions. If a product is out of stock, a clinician or pharmacist decides on any alternative, and the patient is told before anything changes. A different bottle size or format also needs a clinician's approval. Agents never recommend, compare or promote products. Unused or damaged medicine can be taken to any pharmacy for safe disposal.

policy.label: Policy P5.2: Failed payments
policy.text:
If a plan charge fails, we email the patient and try again 2 days and 5 days after the billing date. If the second retry fails, that month's order goes on hold with the reason "Payment failed" until a payment goes through. There are no late fees.

When a patient updates their card in their account, we retry within 1 hour, and a held order goes back to dispensing as soon as the payment succeeds. A failed payment is usually an expired card, a changed card number or a bank block; agents cannot see why a bank declined a charge, and should suggest checking the card details first, then the bank.
